question.problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y)g(x,y),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =x+y,\, &  & ∇f(x,y)=\text{ }i+\text{ }j, &  &  \\ g(x,y) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y),\, &  & ∇g(x,y)=\frac{1}{x+y}\text{ }i+\frac{1}{x+y}\text{ }j. &  & \end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $g(x,y)$ is given by:

$$
∇[fg]=g\,∇\,f+f\,∇\,g
$$

So, using this product rule we obtain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)g(x,y)] & =g(x,y)∇f(x,y)+f(x,y)∇g(x,y) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)(\text{ }i+\text{ }j)+(x+y)(\frac{1}{x+y}\text{ }i+\frac{1}{x+y}\text{ }j) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\text{ }i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\text{ }j+\frac{x+y}{x+y}\text{ }i+\frac{x+y}{x+y}\text{ }j \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\text{ }i+\text{ }i)+(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\text{ }j+1\text{ }j) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)+1)\text{ }i+(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)+1)\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$
